title.narrative: Strengthening Rural Governance for the Right to Adequate Food Phase 2_KENYA

description.narrative: Direct target groups: 21,000 Rights holders at the micro- and meso-levels in the intervention areas: Citizens directly reached through program activities, community members, particularly from marginalized groups.30 Members of Grassroots, Community-based organizations (CBO) and Civil Society Organizations (CSO) at the micro- and meso-levels e.g. Women and Youth groups, Community Social Accountability Committees (CSAC), Community Action Groups (CAG).50 Leaders of these organizations and paralegals whose capacities are strengthened to facilitate social accountability processes.30 Members of CSOs at the national level, who are supported to collaborate as coalition to increase their leverage in advocating for the Right to Food.10 Staff of the civil society partner organizations - implementing partners.40 Intermediaries., journalists, academics, human rights institutions- involved as allies to raise awareness on the Right to Food, take up and disseminate advocacy demands and support advocacy.350 Duty bearers at the micro- and meso-levels in the intervention areas: government representatives, civil servants, local service providers.100 Duty bearers at the national level: government representatives, Members of Parliament, and civil servants, who are sensitized about their role and obligations.Government representatives (including from donor countries) involved in international processes and staff of international bodies, organizations, and platforms (FAO, IFAD, CFS, UNFSS, UN Human Rights System) who will be addressed at the level of the program countries, in Germany and at international events.Indirect target groups: 105,000 people who will be reached through community awareness raising, multipliers in CBOs, dialogue events and media campaigns as well as benefitting from the improvement of public services.

Overall objective (Impact):Progressive governance for the right to food, guided by the principles of participation, transparency, accountability, non-discrimination, and rule of law, for improved food and nutrition security in rural communities.Project purpose (Outcome):Duty bearers in the program countries (Kenya, Malawi, Ethiopia, Zimbabwe) progressively enact and implement inclusive legal frameworks, policies and programs that are conducive to the realization of the right to food and that promote accountability.

The program aims to promote good governance in the rural areas of Vihiga County, with the long-term objective of progressive enactment and implementation of inclusive legal frameworks, policies and programs that contribute to the realization of the right to food and promote accountability. It mobilizes civil society, media, and influencers to pressure decision-makers. National and subnational coalitions on the Right to Food/Food Systems use grassroots evidence to strategically engage in advocacy, creating critical influence and testing approaches before scaling them to meso and macro levels.
